_comment: D-178 release pipeline input — copy to release.config.json (gitignored) per release. `release:build` reads it → dist/release/; `release:publish` uploads to R2. base_url sets each artifact's URL in the manifest, so it MUST match where release:publish uploads: with the recommended flat layout (one bucket at releases.recued.com, --prefix ''), base_url = the domain root, so binaries sit beside manifest.json. For a prefixed/cdn layout, base_url's path must equal release:publish's --prefix (the publisher warns on a mismatch). docker digests must be real (pull is digest-anchored, I-2).
_trap_version: ⛔ `version` MUST equal what the built binary self-reports (backend/server/package.json). If the manifest advertises a version the binary does not claim, a server applies the update, still reports the old version, and is offered the same release again on every check — forever. Under the yy.m.d scheme this bites whenever you date-name a release without bumping package.json first. Bump and rebuild together, or ship the version the tree already has.
_trap_sequence: ⛔ `sequence` is monotonic and effectively irreversible. The anti-replay floor persists PER INSTALL, so once a server has accepted sequence N it refuses anything ≤ N as a replay — a mistakenly-high sequence cannot be walked back remotely, and a reused one is silently ignored by exactly the servers that already updated.
_trap_notes_url: ⛔ Only set `notes_url` if the page exists. It is surfaced as a clickable link in the D-158 update notification, so a 404 here is a dead link pushed to every owner.
_trap_optional: `notes_url`, `docker_baked`, `docker_thin` and the whole `edge` channel are OPTIONAL — omit them rather than shipping placeholders. A `sha256:REPLACE_WITH_REAL_DIGEST` left in place is a digest-anchored pull that can never succeed.
_note_manifest_paths: `base_url` is the ARTIFACT root and must keep matching release:publish's --prefix (that is what the ALIGNMENT warning checks). The MANIFEST is separate: release:publish uploads the signed pair to <base_url>/<channel>/manifest.json for EVERY channel declared below, plus the legacy flat <base_url>/manifest.json. Identical bytes at every path — one signature, one sequence, all channels inside each copy — so verification and anti-replay are unaffected. The split is purely so Cloudflare's path counts can separate a stable fleet from an edge one (stage-gates §2a: 7 req/server/week stable at the 24h cadence, 28 edge at 6h). Adding a channel here automatically adds its manifest path at publish; removing one leaves the old path serving a stale manifest until you delete the object.
